Hi, this message is for Ms. Ito. This is Daniel from the Harbor Grill, calling about your reservation for six people on Thursday at seven thirty. I'm sorry, but our private room is not available that night, so we have a large booth by the window for your group. Our chef asked me to tell you that the kitchen can prepare a menu of small plates to share, and that he can make vegetarian dishes for your guests. Our dress code is business casual, so please ask your guests not to wear shorts or sneakers. If you want to bring your own wine, the corkage fee is thirty dollars per bottle. Please call us back before Wednesday to confirm. Thank you, and have a great day.

Last month, I took a client from Japan to dinner in New York, and I learned a lot. Before we went, my boss told me to choose a quiet place, and she asked me not to order too much food. My client is a picky eater, so I sent him the menu the day before, and I asked him to tell me what he didn't eat. At the restaurant, the waiter asked us to wait ten minutes at the bar, because our table wasn't ready. That was fine, we talked about his family. At the end, my client asked me to let him pay, but I told him that it was my treat. The next morning, I expensed the dinner, and my boss told me to do it again next time. The dinner cost three hundred dollars, and the contract was worth three million.

First, I book a table and ask the restaurant about the dress code. Then, I send the menu to my guests and ask them to tell me what they don't eat. Next, at the restaurant, I order some small plates for the table to share. After that, I make a toast to our partnership. Finally, I pay the bill, keep the receipt, and expense the dinner.
